zoe (support-lead): Heads-up — we just got an escalation from AcmePay. Their product team sees TTFT and tokens/sec flip to negative in the Console for streaming routes and their UI crashes when it tries to render throughput. Screenshot (redacted): https://redwood-internal.screens/ACME-NEG-1

metrics-bot: [ALERT] streaming_metrics.negatives count=4 scope=prod route=rw-stream-1

devon (eng-runtime): Can you paste a repro or request ids? Which route/model and timeframe?

zoe (support-lead): Customer: acmepay_org_42, route: /v1/stream (rw-stream-1). Reported around 2026-03-18 10:11-10:20 UTC. Example request id: req-7c2f9a. Screenshot shows tokens/sec = -14.3 and TTFT = -0.023s.

kevin (support): I pulled Console graph for that org and timeframe — series dips below zero multiple times. Also saw gaps (nulls) before/after dips.

devon (eng-runtime): Paste of a short telemetry snippet we received from the stream-telemetry topic for that req: ```
2026-03-18T10:12:01.000Z telemetry { customer=acmepay_org_42 request=req-7c2f9a tokens_total=1530 event_ts=2026-03-18T10:12:01Z }
2026-03-18T10:12:02.000Z telemetry { customer=acmepay_org_42 request=req-7c2f9a tokens_total=1500 event_ts=2026-03-18T10:12:02Z }
```

devon (eng-runtime): Notice tokens_total decreased between consecutive events -> our rate calc does (t_curr - t_prev) / (ts_curr - ts_prev) and we end up with a negative rate. Need to know why tokens_total decreased.

anya (eng-ml): Two quick possibilities: 1) counters reset (process restart) and we don't detect reset, or 2) out-of-order events / clock skew. If it's reset, increase() style logic handles it. If it's out-of-order, we need to reorder or drop older events.

sam (eng-infra): We had a Kafka upgrade on 2026-03-17 that increased partition leader moves during rolling restart. Preliminary check: stream-telemetry producer uses partition key = hash(sessionId) % 32 (sharded by session), but aggregation is done by customer id. If different sessions for same customer land on different partitions, ordering per-customer is not guaranteed and the consumer (stream-metrics-consumer) reconstructs per-customer timelines and can see older events after newer ones.

devon (eng-runtime): Ah — so root cause might be inconsistent partitioning key between producer and aggregator grouping. That would explain out-of-order tokens_total.

lina (customer-success): Which customers are impacted? I need a list to notify.

zoe (support-lead): I ran a quick query: affected orgs in last 24h: acmepay_org_42, finwave_inc, beta-plays. Low volume but high visibility.

devon (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigations: 
- Update stream-metrics-consumer to clamp negative deltas to 0 when computing tokens/sec (hotfix).
- Update Console queries to use SQL expression that maxes 0 over delta (avoid rendering negatives).
- Add guard in aggregator to drop/reorder events for a per-customer monotonic timeline (longer-term).

anya (eng-ml): For Prometheus-style logic use increase(streaming_tokens_total[1m]) instead of rate() if underlying source can reset. For ClickHouse pipeline, use runningDifference with `max(0, diff)`. Example fix for dashboard query: ```sql
SELECT ts, max(0, runningDifference(sum_tokens)) AS tokens_sec FROM ( ... )
```

devon (eng-runtime): Quick patch we can deploy now: in stream-metrics-consumer PR #584 change tokens_delta = max(0, curr.total - prev.total) and annotate negative occurrences in metric metadata. I'll open the PR.

sam (eng-infra): Also we should change producer partition key to use customer_id (or composite customer+session if we need session locality) so ordering by customer is preserved. That will require a controlled rollout (partitioning change will rebalance).

kevin (support): For customer comms: suggest a short note: we observed incorrect negative values in Console graphs for streaming throughput due to telemetry ordering after broker maintenance; we've fixed display and will deploy a pipeline patch + follow-up partitioning change. ETA for hotfix?

devon (eng-runtime): Hotfix PR opened: #584 (clamp negatives). Targeting canary and prod deploy in next 30m after smoke tests. Backfill plan: identify records where delta<0 and either set to NULL or 0 for rendered metrics and mark as corrected in a correction table. I'll add a backfill script in the PR.

lina (customer-success): I'll draft the customer note and queue it for review once you confirm hotfix deploy time.

anya (eng-ml): Post-mortem items: 
- Make telemetry semantics explicit (counter vs gauge).
- Add tests for out-of-order events and counter resets.
- Add monitoring alert for negative deltas > 0 occurrences.

zoe (support-lead): Creating incident INC-2026-03-18-01 and assigning eng-runtime + eng-infra. I'll update AcmePay and other affected customers once hotfix is live.

metrics-bot: Incident created INC-2026-03-18-01 (sev=3) assignees=[devon,sam]\n
kevin (support): Thanks — keep this thread updated with deploy times and backfill completion.

devon (eng-runtime): Deploy started at 2026-03-18T10:38:00Z -> canary healthy. Prod deploy scheduled for 10:45Z.

zoe (support-lead): Noted. Lina will send initial customer communication after canary looks good.

devon (eng-runtime): Prod deploy complete 2026-03-18T10:46Z. Console now clamps negatives to 0, alert rate for negatives dropped to 0 in last 15m. Backfill queued (ClickHouse job id: ch-backfill-992).

lina (customer-success): Sent update to AcmePay and the other impacted customers at 10:55Z. They acknowledged and will monitor.

zoe (support-lead): Closing loop here — postmortem and follow-ups assigned in INC ticket. Thanks team.
